formula: said (that) + clause · told + person + (that) + clause · tense shifts back one step · asked if / asked + wh-
when_to_use: To report what someone said. The verb usually shifts back one tense (am → was, will → would, is going → was going), and pronouns/time words change. Use 'said' without a person and 'told' WITH a person. Questions become 'asked if' or 'asked + question word' in statement order.
when_to_use_ar: لنقل كلام شخص. الفعل يتراجع زمنًا واحدًا (am→was، will→would)، والضمائر وكلمات الزمن تتغير. 'said' بدون شخص و'told' مع شخص. الأسئلة تصبح asked if أو asked + أداة سؤال بترتيب الجملة الخبرية.
why_arabic_speakers_struggle: Arabic reported speech keeps the original tense (قال إنه متعب), so learners don't backshift ('He said he is tired'). They also mix say/tell ('He said me') and keep question word order ('He asked where is the bank').

examples.en: She told me (that) she would call.
They said they had finished the work.
He asked if I was ready.
She asked where the station was.

common_errors.explanation: Reporting a past statement shifts the tense back one step.

common_errors.wrong: He said me he was busy.
common_errors.correct: He told me he was busy. / He said he was busy.

common_errors.wrong: She asked where is the bank.
common_errors.correct: She asked where the bank was.
common_errors.explanation: Reported questions use statement word order, not inversion.

practice_fill_blank.sentence: "I'll help you." → She ___ me she would help.
"Are you ready?" → He asked ___ I was ready.
"Where do you live?" → She asked where I ___.
"We have finished." → They said they ___ finished.

quick_rule: Shift the tense back one step · say (no person) vs tell (+ person) · reported questions use statement order.
quick_rule_ar: أرجع الزمن خطوة واحدة · say بدون شخص و tell مع شخص · الأسئلة المنقولة بترتيب الجملة الخبرية.
mnemonic: Step the tense back, tell needs a listener, questions lose their inversion.
connect_to_speaking: In accent week 11 you practised weak 'that' and the said/told contrast. Say: 'He said thət he was tired' — 'that' almost disappears; keep 'SAID' and 'TIRED' strong.
